ar_glass_bowl_area.blurb: A small group of sandstone boulders on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, part of the Idaho Boulders zone beneath the north end of the cliff line. Nine problems cover a wide spread, from V0 up through a couple of V7s to two V10s, with the hardest line being the one the area is named for. The boulders sit a short walk to the left of the main trail along the base of the cliffs. The spot is heavily shaded, especially from mid-afternoon on. Other boulders in the zone are close by, so it combines easily with a wider bouldering day.

ar_autobahn_boulder.blurb: One of the boulders in the Patio Boulders group near Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas, and the one furthest down the slope. Its steep south face is covered in holds and catches sun for most of the day. Eight problems run from V0 to V5, with several in the V3 to V4 range, and the V5 here is regarded as one of the better lines of that grade in the state. Most boulders in the surrounding group also face south, so it is a good choice when the weather is cool. Reach it by following the trail past the Plaque Wall Boulder and continuing downhill.

ar_tool_buttress_the.blurb: A small buttress in the Middle East section of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch's east side, in north-central Arkansas. It holds eight roped routes, mostly bolted sport lines with two trad climbs, ranging from 5.7 up to the low 5.12s, with a cluster of 5.10 to 5.11 in between. A few of the harder lines here are seldom visited yet well regarded. The wall is sunny, so cooler months suit it better than summer, and there are boulders nearby. Expect thick underbrush on the way in, and few other people in this part of the canyon.

ar_afterthought_boulder.blurb: A single boulder in the Shingles Area on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, north-central Arkansas, covered in honeycomb-like features. It has eight problems, nearly all easy: several at VB to V0, one V1 and a V3 traverse, which makes it a gentle stop for newer boulderers or a warm-up. The holds are good, though the tops can be mossy, so bring a brush. It sits beside the main ranch track on the right, just across from the Shingles Boulder, and is quick to find.
ar_afterthought_boulder.approach: Follow the main ranch track uphill to the zip-line. The boulder is on the right, across from the Shingles Boulder.

ar_undertow_boulder.blurb: An overhanging sandstone boulder on the east side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, with pockets and an arete among its lines. Eight problems climb from V1 through a V4 pair to a run of V7s and V8s, so most of the difficulty is at the top end and the area suits strong boulderers. The east side is known for bouldering that is spread out, and the walk in can be long depending on where you leave the car.
